note: Every tool is served at POST /api/tools/<name> and over MCP at /mcp. Screens call the same tools.

tools.name: chat.list_channels
tools.title: List channels
tools.description: The channels and direct messages you are in, with unread and mention counts. browse: true adds public channels you have not joined.

browse.description: Also list public channels you are not in

tools.name: chat.get_channel
tools.title: Open a channel
tools.description: One channel: its topic, who is in it, your notification rule for it and its unread count.

channel.description: A channel: its name (general, #general) or id

tools.name: chat.read
tools.title: Read messages
tools.description: Messages in a channel, oldest first (the latest 50 by default; before gives older ones). Give thread instead to read one thread: its first message and every reply.

channel.description: A channel: its name (general, #general) or id

thread.description: Read this thread instead of the channel

before.description: Only messages older than this id

after.description: Only messages newer than this id

tools.name: chat.search
tools.title: Search messages
tools.description: Find messages by words, in every channel you can see. Narrow with channel and from, or write in:#channel and from:@person among the words.

channel.description: A channel: its name (general, #general) or id

from.description: Only messages from this person (handle or name)

tools.name: chat.list_mentions
tools.title: Mentions
tools.description: Messages that mention you, newest first.

tools.name: chat.list_people
tools.title: List people and agents
tools.description: Everyone on the team, people and agents, with handles to @mention and their status. me is you.

tools.name: chat.list_events
tools.title: What changed
tools.description: Everything that happened since a cursor: new, edited and deleted messages, reactions, channel changes. Returns a new cursor. Screens use it to catch up after being away, and as the live feed when WebSockets are not available.

since.description: The cursor from the last call (0 or empty: start from now)

tools.name: chat.get_settings
tools.title: Your settings
tools.description: Your notification rule, keywords, theme, push devices, the server push key, and whether agents have a real model.

tools.name: chat.post
tools.title: Post a message
tools.description: Post a message to a channel or direct message. Markdown works. @handle mentions someone (and wakes an agent); @channel tells everyone in it. files: ids from chat.upload_file.

channel.description: A channel: its name (general, #general) or id

tools.name: chat.reply
tools.title: Reply in a thread
tools.description: Reply in the thread of a message (any message in the thread works). Mention an agent here and it answers in the same thread.

tools.name: chat.edit
tools.title: Edit a message
tools.description: Change the words of one of your own messages.

tools.name: chat.delete
tools.title: Delete a message
tools.description: Delete one of your messages (admins can delete anyone's). The words are wiped. Only when the person clearly asks.

tools.name: chat.react
tools.title: React
tools.description: Add an emoji reaction to a message, or take yours off with remove: true.

tools.name: chat.upload_file
tools.title: Upload a file
tools.description: Upload a file (as base64) to attach to a message with chat.post or chat.reply. The screens stream files to /files instead; this is the same thing for agents.

tools.name: chat.set_typing
tools.title: Typing
tools.description: Tell others in a channel (or thread) that you are typing. Lasts a few seconds; nothing is stored.

channel.description: A channel: its name (general, #general) or id

tools.name: chat.create_channel
tools.title: Create a channel
tools.description: Make a channel. Public channels anyone on the team can find and join; private ones only invited people see.

name.description: Lowercase, dashes for spaces, like launch-plans

tools.name: chat.open_dm
tools.title: Message someone directly
tools.description: Open (or find) a direct message with one person or agent, or a group message with up to 8. Then post to it with chat.post.

tools.name: chat.invite
tools.title: Add people to a channel
tools.description: Add people or agents to a channel you are in. Adding an agent lets it answer when mentioned there.

channel.description: A channel: its name (general, #general) or id

tools.name: chat.join
tools.title: Join a channel
tools.description: Join a public channel.

channel.description: A channel: its name (general, #general) or id

tools.name: chat.leave
tools.title: Leave a channel
tools.description: Leave a channel. You can rejoin a public one any time; a private one needs an invite.

channel.description: A channel: its name (general, #general) or id

tools.name: chat.set_topic
tools.title: Set the topic
tools.description: Set or clear (empty) the one-line topic shown at the top of a channel.

channel.description: A channel: its name (general, #general) or id

tools.name: chat.archive_channel
tools.title: Archive a channel
tools.description: Archive a channel: it stays readable and searchable but nobody can post. archived: false brings it back.

channel.description: A channel: its name (general, #general) or id

tools.name: chat.set_status
tools.title: Set your status
tools.description: Set your status line and emoji, like "In meetings" 📅. Empty clears it.

tools.name: chat.add_person
tools.title: Add someone to the team
tools.description: Let someone sign in: by GitHub username, by email (for the email link), or both. They join #general.

tools.name: chat.remove_person
tools.title: Remove someone from the team
tools.description: Take someone off the team: they are signed out and leave every channel. Their messages stay. An agent calling this asks a person first.

tools.name: chat.add_agent
tools.title: Add an agent
tools.description: Add an AI agent as a team member. It answers in the thread when @mentioned in a channel it is in, or when messaged directly. It uses the server's model (CHAT_MODEL_URL, CHAT_MODEL_KEY, CHAT_MODEL) unless you give it its own.

tools.name: chat.mark_read
tools.title: Mark as read
tools.description: Mark a channel read, up to the newest message or up to a given message.

channel.description: A channel: its name (general, #general) or id

tools.name: chat.mark_unread
tools.title: Mark unread
tools.description: Mark a channel unread from a message on, to come back to it later.

tools.name: chat.set_notify
tools.title: Notification rule
tools.description: When to be notified. For one channel: all, mentions, none, or default (follow your own rule). Without a channel: your own rule for every channel, all, mentions or none. Direct messages always notify unless set to none.

channel.description: A channel: its name (general, #general) or id

tools.name: chat.set_preferences
tools.title: Preferences
tools.description: Your preferences: theme (auto, light, dark), push (true or false: phone and desktop notifications), keywords (words that notify you anywhere).

tools.name: chat.subscribe_push
tools.title: Turn on notifications on this device
tools.description: Save a browser push subscription so mentions and direct messages reach this device. The browser asks the person first; an agent cannot click that.

tools.name: chat.unsubscribe_push
tools.title: Turn off notifications on a device
tools.description: Stop push notifications to one device (its endpoint) or, without one, to all your devices.

tools.name: chat.list_approvals
tools.title: Waiting for your yes
tools.description: Things an agent asked to do that need your yes first.

tools.name: chat.decide_approval
tools.title: Approve or decline
tools.description: Say yes or no to something an agent asked to do. Yes runs it as you.

tools.name: chat.export
tools.title: Export everything
tools.description: Export every channel, message, reaction, file and person as a zip in the Slack export layout (plus a lossless wos/ folder). Returns a download link.

tools.name: chat.import_slack
tools.title: Import from Slack
tools.description: Preview a Slack export zip (uploaded with chat.upload_file): who and what it holds, and what Slack left out. Bringing it in lands in v1; for now this previews only.
